correctness.rationale: For all integer m>=1 and p>=0, normalized true-level Hermite modes have angular frequency p−1. Angular selection gives exactly one target e_(p+m); the Gaussian t-integral evaluates by Gamma recurrence to Gamma(p+m/2)[p−m(m−2)/4], including p=0. The factor vanishes at an integer nonnegative p iff m is even, at p=m(m−2)/4. Gamma-ratio asymptotics prove weights tend to one with coefficient −3m²/(8p), so the operator has closed range, dim ker 0 or 1, cokernel m+ker, Fredholm index −m, essential spectrum circle and full closed-disk spectrum. A standalone checker passed 1551 diagnostics including eight quadratures, but infinite statements follow analytically.

value.rationale: Pure angular winding is the canonical unimodular phase observable, and the second Landau level is the minimal Gaussian polyanalytic setting permitting radial nodal cancellation. The theorem gives a complete exact classification of every winding, showing a counterintuitive parity-dependent one-dimensional lost channel invisible to the stable index and essential spectrum. These are natural operator-theoretic invariants rather than a parameter slice or numerical curiosity.
